title: Generalization of Transformer-Based Neural Quantum States via In-Context Learning
authors: Zhen Qin, Qing Qu, Alfred O. Hero
abstract: Neural quantum states based on modern deep learning architectures have emerged as powerful representations for quantum many-body systems. In particular, Transformer-based neural quantum states provide expressive models capable of capturing long-range correlations, and their empirical generalization performance has recently been demonstrated. However, a theoretical understanding of their generalization behavior remains largely unexplored. In this paper, we develop a theoretical framework to analyze the generalization properties of Transformer-based neural quantum states under in-context learning. We establish a rigorous inference-time generalization error bound in terms of mean squared error (MSE), showing that the pointwise prediction error decreases inversely with both the number of in-context examples and the depth of the Transformer. We further show that the Transformer depth required to achieve this guarantee scales only linearly with the system size--namely, the number of particles in continuous systems or the number of qudits in discrete systems. Building on this result, we extend our analysis to full quantum states formulated as rank-one density operators, and derive MSE-based generalization bounds over both continuous and discrete domains under physical constraints. Finally, numerical simulations corroborate our theoretical analysis.
summary: This paper provides a theoretical framework to analyze the generalization capability of Transformer-based Neural Quantum States (NQS) under in-context learning. It derives rigorous error bounds showing that prediction accuracy improves predictably with more context examples and deeper networks. This advances the field by providing mathematical guarantees for using advanced deep learning architectures to model complex quantum many-body physics.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop a theoretical understanding of how well Transformer-based neural quantum states generalize when trained using in-context learning (ICL).
main_result: It establishes rigorous generalization error bounds for the pointwise prediction error and extends this to full quantum states, showing the required Transformer depth scales only linearly with system size.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework using Mean Squared Error (MSE) bounds, adapting the established ICL analysis from language models to the quantum state representation.
model_or_system: The model uses Neural Quantum States (NQS) parameterized by a Transformer architecture to represent quantum many-body wavefunctions. These states can describe both continuous systems (e.g., $\psi(\mathbf{x})$ on $(\mathbb{R}^D)^n$) and discrete systems (e.g., spin systems).
key_observables: Pointwise prediction error and MSE-based generalization error bounds for the quantum state.
important_parameters: The number of in-context examples ($N$) and the depth of the Transformer are key parameters governing the error bounds.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the quantum state can be effectively represented by a Transformer and that the generalization error can be bounded using MSE metrics derived from ICL principles.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the entire ICL framework, detailing the flow from input embedding through masked multi-head self-attention and feed-forward layers to the final output prediction.
paper_structure: The paper first analyzes the pointwise prediction error, deriving bounds based on ICL. It then extends this analysis to full quantum states formulated as rank-one density operators, deriving MSE bounds for both continuous and discrete domains, and concludes with numerical simulations.
why_interesting: This work provides crucial theoretical guarantees for using deep learning models like Transformers to simulate complex quantum many-body systems, addressing a major bottleneck in applying modern AI techniques to quantum physics.

figures.caption: Figure 1: In-Context Learning Framework for Transformer-Based Neural Quantum States.

Figure 2: Comparison of generalization errors of Transformer-based neural quantum states in the continuous case over 500 training epochs with Transformer width 64: (a) varying L and N with n = 4 and c = 2, (b) varying n and N with c = 2 and L = 2, (c) varying c and N with n = 4 and L = 2. These results empirically validate the theoretical scaling law in (19): the generalization error decreases with the number of in-context samples N and increases with the problem dimension n and energy constraint B, while exhibiting an approximately linear dependence on (log L)/L.

Figure 3: Comparison of generalization errors of Transformer-based neural quantum states in the discrete case with Transformer width 32: (a) varying n and L with S = 128, (b) varying L and S with n = 5 and 500 training epochs. These results demonstrate that the generalization error decreases with increasing model depth and the number of in- context samples, while increasing with system size n, consistent with the scaling behavior predicted by the theoretical analysis.

Figure 4: Comparison of the generalization error for predicting unknown linear observables as the number of qubits n varies. The Transformer width is fixed at 64 and the number of layers is fixed at L = 4. Results are obtained after 300 training epochs (32 batches per epoch) and evaluated on 100 testing tasks. These results demonstrate the predicted benefit of increasing the number of in-context samples N and the increasing difficulty of the prediction task with system size n, consistent with the theoretical bounds in (29) and (30).
